channel.title: CRGD: The Public Policy Bridge: publications
channel.description: New research, analysis and commentary from Centre for Research on Governance and Development.

item.title: The Port Is Built. Now Build the Town Around It.
item.dc:creator: scholar-two
item.description: A transhipment port creates few jobs by itself. Whether Thiruvananthapuram benefits depends on the logistics, housing, skills and services that grow around it, and on planning that starts now.

item.title: The Public Policy Bridge: Essays on Governing Kerala
item.dc:creator: scholar-one
item.description: A forthcoming edited volume bringing together essays by CRGD researchers and invited contributors on the central questions of governing Kerala in the coming decades.

item.title: Bringing Off Budget Borrowing into the Light
item.dc:creator: scholar-one
item.description: Borrowing by state owned bodies has become a large and contested part of public finance. A simple annual disclosure statement would let legislators and citizens see the full picture without stopping investment.

item.title: Five Books for Anyone Starting Out in Indian Public Policy
item.dc:creator: mentor-one
item.description: Fellows and interns often ask where to begin. Here is a short reading list, chosen for clarity, range and the arguments they will provoke.

item.title: What Three Decades of Decentralisation Have Taught Us
item.dc:creator: adviser-one
item.description: A practitioner reflects on what Kerala's experiment in local democracy achieved, what it did not, and what the next generation of reform should look like.

item.title: A Care Guarantee for Older Citizens
item.dc:creator: fellow-one
item.description: Kerala is ageing faster than most of India, and many older people live without younger family nearby. Local governments are well placed to guarantee a basic level of care.

item.title: Kerala Needs a Fiscal Conversation, Not a Blame Game
item.dc:creator: adviser-two
item.description: Every argument about the state's finances turns into an argument about who is to blame. The public deserves a debate about choices instead.

item.title: The Bridge, Episode 1: What Is a Think Tank For?
item.dc:creator: researcher-one
item.description: In the first episode of CRGD's podcast, the team talks about why the institution was created, what a think tank can and cannot do, and why it is based in Thiruvananthapuram.

item.title: The Gulf Comes Home: Return Migration and Kerala's Next Economy
item.dc:creator: associate-one, scholar-two
item.description: For half a century, work in the Gulf has shaped Kerala's households, towns and politics. As more migrants return, the state faces a question it has rarely had to answer: what will they do here?

item.title: Why Bus Ridership Matters More Than Metro Ridership
item.dc:creator: fellow-two
item.description: Metro lines attract attention and investment. Buses carry far more people in Kerala, and their decline deserves at least as much concern.

item.title: Panchayat Finances After Three Decades of Decentralisation
item.dc:creator: scholar-one, intern-one
item.description: Kerala transferred real money and power to local governments in the 1990s. This report examines how local finances have evolved since, and what would strengthen them for the next thirty years.

item.title: Why My Generation Is Leaving, and What Might Make Us Stay
item.dc:creator: intern-two
item.description: Half my class is planning to study or work abroad. A student's view of why, and of what the state could do about it.

item.title: Five Steps Towards Halving Road Deaths
item.dc:creator: fellow-two
item.description: Road crashes kill and injure thousands of people in Kerala every year, most of them pedestrians, cyclists and riders of two wheelers. Proven measures exist. This brief sets out five.

item.title: Women's Work Is Kerala's Missing Growth Engine
item.dc:creator: fellow-one
item.description: A state that educates its daughters as well as Kerala does, and then loses their talent to the labour market, is leaving its most important growth opportunity unused.

item.title: After the Landslides: Building Safer Hill Communities
item.dc:creator: researcher-three, scholar-three, fellow-two
item.description: Landslides in Kerala's hill districts have taken many lives in recent years. This special report brings together geology, land use, local governance and the experience of survivors to set out how hill communities can be made safer.

item.title: Mapping Household Waste Collection in an Urban Ward: Methods and Lessons
item.dc:creator: intern-two, fellow-two
item.description: An internship project that set out to map how household waste is collected, sorted and transported in one urban ward, and what the process revealed about the system.

item.title: The Sea Wall and the Shore
item.dc:creator: scholar-two, researcher-three
item.description: Along much of Kerala's coast, homes, roads and boats face the sea with less beach every year. The responses chosen now will shape the coast for a century.

item.title: Explainer: How the Finance Commission Shares Tax Revenue Among States
item.dc:creator: scholar-one
item.description: Every five years, a commission decides how a large share of India's tax revenue is divided between the Union and the states, and among the states. Here is how it works.

item.title: From Classroom to Career: Graduate Employability in Kerala
item.dc:creator: researcher-one, associate-one
item.description: Kerala educates its young people to a high level, yet many graduates struggle to find work that matches their qualifications. This report traces the gap between what colleges teach and what employers need.

item.title: How We Choose Our Research Questions
item.dc:creator: scholar-one
item.description: There are far more important questions than any institution can answer. A note on how CRGD decides what to work on, and how you can suggest a question.

item.title: What the Data Can and Cannot Tell Us About Women's Work
item.dc:creator: associate-one
item.description: Headlines about women's employment often rest on surveys that count some kinds of work and miss others. A guide to reading the numbers carefully.

item.title: Explainer: What Does a Panchayat Actually Do?
item.dc:creator: researcher-one
item.description: Panchayats run schools, health centres, roads and welfare programs in your neighbourhood. A plain language guide to what they do and how you can take part.

item.title: What a Mock Assembly Taught Me About Real Democracy
item.dc:creator: intern-one
item.description: A day spent debating a bill as a pretend legislator changed how one student thinks about politics.

item.title: The State Budget in Ten Minutes
item.dc:creator: scholar-one
item.description: A short video guide to reading the state budget, covering committed expenditure, deficits, capital spending and borrowing outside the budget.

item.title: Five Questions to Ask of Any State Budget
item.dc:creator: scholar-one
item.description: Budget speeches are full of announcements. The numbers tell a quieter story. Here are five questions that reveal what a budget actually commits the state to.

item.title: Review: Reading the State's Annual Economic Review
item.dc:creator: contributor-two
item.description: Each year the State Planning Board publishes a detailed review of the economy alongside the budget. It is the most useful document few people read. A guide to its strengths and gaps.
